//dependencies: NOT ONE of the foundations demo's own entries was changed by the Passport
migration — same names, same ranges — and they still serve `src/`, `test/`,
and `scripts/` at the repository root.
FOUR NAMES WERE ADDED, and they are resolution control rather than code this
repository imports: compact-js, midnight-js-protocol, midnight-js-utils, and
midnight-js-fetch-zk-config-provider, all pinned to the LEDGER-8 versions
this repository's own tree already resolved transitively. Removing them does
not remove a dependency; it moves one, and the paragraphs below are why that
matters enough to write four lines of manifest about it.
Two Midnight stacks live here at once. The root set below is LEDGER-8
(midnight-js 4.x, compact-runtime 0.16.x, ledger-v8 8.x), shared by the
foundations demo and by `examples/passport-funder`, which asks for the same
names at exact versions inside the same ranges. `examples/passport-demo` is
on LEDGER-9 (wallet-sdk 2.0.0-beta.2, midnight-js 5.0.0-beta.6,
compact-runtime 0.18.0-rc.1) because that is what stagenet runs.
npm hoists one copy of each name to the root and nests the rest. The demo
declares its whole ledger-9 set explicitly, so those nest under
`examples/passport-demo/node_modules` — but only for names the root also
claims. A ledger-9 package with no ledger-8 counterpart at the root gets
hoisted instead, and then nests its OWN copy of compact-runtime 0.18.0-rc.1
beside it. Measured on this tree before the four pins were added: THREE
physical copies of compact-runtime 0.18.0-rc.1, under compact-js, under
midnight-js-protocol, and under the demo. With them: one.
Why that is fatal rather than untidy. A generated Compact contract module
opens with `import * as __compactRuntime from '@midnight-ntwrk/
compact-runtime'` and then `__compactRuntime.checkRuntimeVersion('<exact
version>')`. Node and the bundler both resolve that specifier from the
MODULE's directory, walking upwards — so which copy a contract gets is
decided by where the contract file sits, not by which workspace asked for
it. And midnight-js decodes contract state through `ChargedState`: two
copies of the runtime are two `ChargedState` classes, and an `instanceof`
check then fails on objects that are correct in every other respect. Two
copies of compact-js are two `CompactContext` TypeId symbols, and
`deployContract` dies with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading
'ctor')` — measured against stagenet on 2026/08/24.
So: keep this list and `examples/passport-funder`'s dependencies at
compatible versions, keep `examples/passport-demo`'s ledger-9 list
internally consistent, and do not promote either stack's packages to the
root one at a time.
//overrides: Added by the Passport migration. Three entries, each of which reaches
resolution the foundations demo already had, so each says what it changes
and why it is safe.
`@scure/base` 2.3.0. THE ONE THAT IS LOAD BEARING FOR CORRECTNESS. A freshly
resolved tree picks 2.4.0, which reimposes bech32's classic 90-character
limit on bech32m. Midnight's shielded addresses are 133 characters, so
`MidnightBech32m.parse` throws 'invalid string length 133, expected (8..90)'
and the app reports a valid stagenet shielded address as 'not a Midnight
address'. Caught here by e2e/send-assets.spec.ts, and reproduced outside the
browser on both trees before pinning. 2.3.0 is the version the live site was
built and deployed against; the foundations demo resolved 2.2.0 before this
and its own gates pass on 2.3.0.
`@midnight-ntwrk/wallet-sdk-utilities` 1.2.1. Nothing declares this
directly — it arrives transitively on both sides. wallet-sdk 2.0.0-beta.2
pins 1.2.0, a publish that does not export `Clock`; wallet-sdk-facade
imports `Clock`, so the wallet dies at build time with the rollup error
'Clock is not exported by …/wallet-sdk-utilities/dist/index.js'. 1.2.1 is
the fixed publish and is otherwise identical.
It is written GLOBALLY, which is the blunt form, because both surgical forms
were tried against this tree and neither reaches the copy that matters.
`"…-utilities@1.2.0": "1.2.1"` (by requested version) and
`{"@midnight-ntwrk/wallet-sdk": {"@midnight-ntwrk/wallet-sdk-utilities":
"1.2.1"}}` (scoped to the parent) both leave 1.2.0 inside
node_modules/@midnight-ntwrk/wallet-sdk/node_modules, which is exactly where
the beta tree lives and where the broken copy is.
A fourth override, pinning `@midnight-ntwrk/ledger-v8` to 8.0.3, was carried
over from the source repository and then DROPPED: npm refuses an override
that disagrees with a root direct dependency, and this root declares
ledger-v8 at `^8.0.3`. It was a drift guard for `examples/passport-funder`,
which pins 8.0.3 exactly and gets its own nested copy here anyway — verified
in the resolved tree. If the funder's typecheck ever starts reporting
'ZswapSecretKeys is not assignable to ZswapSecretKeys', this is the cause
and the fix is to narrow the root range, not to add the override back.
